transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I, uh… I’m here because I lost my temper on a board call. It was over a small question about the facility budget, and I snapped at someone. That’s not how I run my company, or how I treat people.
Has this kind of emotional reaction happened before, or was this the first time you've lost your temper in such a way?
This was the first time it got like that. I mean, I’ve been annoyed before, sure, but snapping on a board call over something that small… that’s not like me.
Have you been experiencing any other emotional changes or difficulties recently, especially around the time of that board call?

A little, yes. Things that normally steady me… chess problems, going through my hiking notes, dinner with my wife… they just feel kind of flat right now. Like I know I should enjoy them, but I can’t quite get there.
Has this feeling of things feeling flat or unenjoyable happened before, or is this something new and different for you?
It’s new. I mean… I’ve had bad weeks before, but this feels different. The usual things—chess, my hiking notes, dinner with my wife—they just don’t land the way they should. It’s all kind of flat.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting pleasure from those activities anymore, or do you just feel like you should enjoy them but can’t?
I guess it’s more that I know I should enjoy them, but I don’t really feel it. The chess, my hiking notes, even dinner with my wife… it just feels flat. Like I can’t quite get there.
Has this loss of enjoyment in your usual activities, like chess or dinner with your wife, been happening every day for at least two weeks?
No… not two weeks. It’s been about six days, I think. Since the explosion and fire during the walkthrough.
Since the fire during the walkthrough, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels, or have you been feeling more down or hopeless than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track of all that. I mean… I feel off, but I don’t know that I’d call it hopeless or anything. Sleep and appetite… I don’t know. Nothing I can say clearly.
Can you tell me more about the fire during the walkthrough? How did it affect you emotionally at the time?

I don’t really know how to talk about it. It was… sudden. Loud. I remember being scared, I guess. Mostly just trying to get through it and make sure people were moving. I didn’t really stop to feel much right then.
Since the fire during the walkthrough, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy, beyond just feeling like they're flat?

Yeah… I guess so. I try to do a chess problem, or look at my hiking notes, and it just doesn’t… land. Dinner with my wife too. I know those things usually settle me, but right now they just feel flat. I can’t really get to the good part of it.
Since the fire during the walkthrough, have you found yourself thinking about it more than you want to, or has it been coming back to your mind even when you’re trying to focus on something else?
Yeah… it does come back. I’ll be on a call, or looking at numbers, and then that blast and the fire by the loading area just… jumps in my head. Like a bad film I didn’t ask to see.
Since the fire during the walkthrough, have you found yourself avoiding any places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yes. I haven’t gone back to the new building. I keep finding reasons not to.

And there’s paperwork too—the mortgage folder, the safety reports. They’re just sitting there. When I reach for them, my stomach drops, so I leave them.
Since the fire during the walkthrough, have you noticed that you’ve been more jumpy, easily startled, or on edge than usual?

Yeah. More than I’d like.

If a door slams, or the printer starts up behind me, I jump… like something went off again. Takes a few minutes before my hands feel steady.

Has the feeling of things feeling flat or not enjoying your usual activities, like chess or dinner with your wife, been happening almost every day for the past two weeks, or has it been less consistent than that?

Almost every day, I guess.

Chess, my hiking notes… dinner with my wife. They’re there, but it all feels kind of flat. Like I know I should enjoy it, but I just… don’t quite get there.
Since the fire during the walkthrough, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight?
Not really. I mean… I haven’t been tracking it closely, but I don’t think my weight’s changed much. Appetite seems about the same, I guess.
Since the fire during the walkthrough, have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual?
I don’t think so. I mean… I’ve gone over it in my head, sure, but I wouldn’t say I’m blaming myself more than usual.
Since the fire during the walkthrough, have you found that you no longer care about doing things you used to care about, even things that used to be important to you?

Yeah… I guess so. Not that I don’t care at all, but things that usually settle me — chess, my hiking notes, dinner with my wife — they just feel flat right now. Like I know I should enjoy them, but I can’t quite get there.
How many days out of the past two weeks have you felt down, depressed, or lost interest in things because of the fire during the walkthrough?
About six days, I think. Since the explosion and fire happened.
Since the fire during the walkthrough, have you noticed that you no longer take the same interest in things you used to care about, even activities that were important to you before?
Yeah… I think I already said, it’s just sort of flat. Chess problems, my hiking notes, even dinner with my wife — I know those things should matter to me, but lately I can’t really feel it.
Since the fire during the walkthrough, have you felt like you can’t experience any pleasure or joy in activities you used to enjoy, like chess, hiking, or having dinner with your wife?

Yeah… I mean, I can still sit there and do the chess problem or look at my hiking notes, but it doesn’t really… land. Dinner with my wife too. It just feels flat, like I should enjoy it, but I can’t quite get there.
